Article Title: In 2012, NFL legend Joe Thomas bought a 1,200-acre Wisconsin farm with five cows and a bull; 14 years later, Hall of Fame Farms spans 4,100 acres and raises hundreds of cattle, including Wagyu
Article Text:
From football to farming

A different kind of Hall of Fame career

What happens on the farm

Building something beyond football

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Cleveland Browns star Joe Thomas has taken an unexpected turn after retiring from football, trading the NFL field for life on a Wisconsin farm. The Pro Football Hall of Famer is the owner of Hall of Fame Farms, a cattle operation located in the state’s Driftless Region. Thomas spent 11 seasons with the Browns before retiring in 2018 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame in 2023. According to Fox News, his interest in farming grew while he was still playing, eventually leading him to build a substantial agricultural operation with his family. Farm Progress has also reported on Thomas’ work on the farm and his approach to raising cattle.Thomas, who grew up in Wisconsin, has spoken about wanting to own land long before his NFL career ended. He purchased the original property in 2012, while still playing for Cleveland, and initially started with just a handful of cattle.What began as a family farm eventually developed into a much larger agricultural operation. Fox News reported in September 2026 that the property has grown from the original 1,200 acres to roughly 4,100 acres and now includes hundreds of cattle, with Wagyu increasingly becoming a focus of the business.The transition also reflects a broader change in Thomas’ life after football. Following his retirement, he became increasingly interested in food, nutrition and the way cattle are raised. Farm Progress reported earlier this year that Thomas and his farm team emphasize nutrition and individual attention when caring for the herd.Thomas’ football résumé gives the farm its distinctive name. Selected third overall by the Cleveland Browns in the 2007 NFL Draft, he played his entire 11-season career in Cleveland. The numbers remain remarkable. Thomas made 10 consecutive Pro Bowls, earned six first-team All-Pro selections and played 10,363 consecutive offensive snaps. The Pro Football Hall of Fame lists him as a member of its Class of 2023.That reputation for consistency has now become part of the identity of his agricultural business. Hall of Fame Farms presents the operation as a long-term family project rather than simply a celebrity venture, with Thomas and his wife, Annie, raising their children around the farm.The cattle operation places a significant emphasis on producing both Wagyu and Certified Angus beef varieties. As reported by Hall of Fame Farms, the cattle are raised on pasture before entering a corn-finishing phase, while the farm also utilizes carefully selected genetics combined with a tailored nutrition programme that was developed in collaboration with a dedicated cattle nutritionist. In addition to this, the company proudly claims to work with Full Blood Wagyu genetics, ensuring high-quality meat production.The approach taken by the farm is fundamentally centred around low-stress handling techniques and a strong focus on comprehensive animal care to promote the well-being of the cattle. As highlighted by Farm Progress, Thomas’ dedicated team prioritizes nutritional needs and provides personalized care for each individual animal within their herd. Currently, the business offers a diverse array of beef products to consumers, which includes a selection of Wagyu steaks, Certified Angus beef, a variety of smoked meats, and beef tallow. Furthermore, the farm has established an online platform that enables customers to conveniently order specific cuts of meat directly from the brand.For Thomas, the world of farming signifies not merely a definitive closure to his athletic career but rather the beginning of a revitalizing second chapter. The meticulous precision and unwavering consistency that characterized his tenure in the NFL have seamlessly transitioned into the philosophy he employs in his cattle operations.Additionally, the backdrop is critical to the entire undertaking. Hall of Fame Farms is nestled within the picturesque rolling hills and lush pasturelands of Wisconsin’s Driftless Region, where Thomas has steadily transformed a property acquired during his football years into a thriving, family-operated agricultural enterprise.Though his storied football career concluded in 2018, the journey into farming has continued to flourish and develop. What commenced with just a modest herd of cattle has blossomed into a noteworthy farming operation in Wisconsin, providing the former Browns tackle with a fresh platform to cultivate the legacy he once strived to establish on the football field.
Article Summary: Former cleveland browns star joe thomas has taken an unexpected turn after retiring from football. The pro football hall of famer is the owner of hall of fame farms, a cattle operation located in the state’s driftless region. Thomas spent 11 seasons with the browns before retiring in 2018.

Article Title: Greatest Family Inspiration: How LeBron James’ daughter Zhuri gave Savannah James the reason to pursue her latest business venture
Article Text:
LeBron James’ daughter Zhuri inspired Savannah James to invest in women’s volleyball. Image via: IMAGO / ABACAPRESS

Savannah James credits daughter Zhuri for inspiring her women’s volleyball investment

Savannah James joins Issa Rae as investor in League One Volleyball team

Who is Savannah James?

All about LeBron and Savannah James’ daughter Zhuri Nova

Savannah James’ investment in women’s volleyball has a personal reason. Her daughter, Zhuri James inspired Savanna to invest in the team. Savannah recently became an investor in LOVB Los Angeles, a professional League One Volleyball team, joining an ownership group that includes Alexis Ohanian and Issa Rae . For Savannah, the move is about more than becoming part of a new sports venture. It connects directly to the sport her youngest child has embraced.Zhuri has already developed a connection with LOVB after attending the league’s championship event and delivering the ceremonial first serve. Now, with LOVB Los Angeles preparing for its first season in 2026-27, Savannah sees an opportunity to support both her daughter and the wider growth of women’s volleyball.Savannah James did not need to look far for a reason to invest in LOVB Los Angeles. Her daughter’s experience with volleyball gave the decision a personal meaning.In a statement, Savannah explained how watching Zhuri play has shaped her view of the sport.“I’ve seen firsthand through my daughter Zhuri how powerful volleyball can be for young girls, the confidence, discipline and sense of community it creates,” Savannah said.The perspective has become central to Savannah’s decision to join the ownership group.She sees the investment as a way to help create a pathway for girls who want to follow the same sport.“I’m excited to be part of LOVB Los Angeles and to help build something special that girls like Zhuri can aspire to be part of one day.”Savannah also spoke about the decision in an Instagram post, making clear that Zhuri’s involvement with volleyball was a major factor.“It was important to me to make my investment with LOVB Los Angeles because my daughter is a volleyball player,” she said. “She is coming up alongside amazing athletes who deserve the recognition that they are getting right now.”She continued, “So, any chance that I have to be able to support that or stand behind it and do things that matter in that way, I am 1000% involved.”Zhuri already has a connection with LOVB. In April, she delivered the first serve at the LOVB Volleyball Championship in Long Beach, California, and later interviewed professional volleyball player Skylar Fields.Her involvement also stands out because basketball has been such a major part of the James family. LeBron James , Bronny James and Bryce James have all been connected to basketball, but Zhuri has taken a different sporting path.LeBron acknowledged that earlier this year when discussing his daughter’s basketball ability.“She’s a volleyball player, don’t get my wife mad,” he said. “My wife is done with basketball, she’s done with it.”LeBron also admitted that Zhuri has still absorbed plenty from growing up around basketball.“[Zhuri’s] a volleyball player. But she’s been around the game for a while, so she does got good handles and she’s good form, too. But my wife ain’t playing that. Not another one. She says that’s it.”For Savannah, the investment gives her a direct way to support something that has already become important to her daughter.Savannah is joining an ownership group led by Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian through his investment firm, Seven Seven Six. The group also includes Issa Rae, adding another prominent name to the ownership side of LOVB Los Angeles.Savannah shared her excitement about working alongside the group in an Instagram post.“So excited to be alongside Issa Rae and Alexis Ohanian in this journey,” James expressed.The investment comes ahead of LOVB Los Angeles’ first season. The team is scheduled to begin play during the league’s 2026-27 season, with home games set for the Intuit Dome in Inglewood, California.The franchise is also preparing for its connection with fans before the season begins. A Fan Fest is scheduled for Sept. 26, giving players an opportunity to meet supporters before the new campaign.Savannah also highlighted what the team already has in place, pointing to its coaching staff and playing roster.“We have amazing coaches, Olympic-level athletes, a roster that can’t be beat, honestly. So, so excited for you guys to join us this season,” she continued.Savannah James, born Savannah Brinson on Aug. 27, 1986, in Akron, Ohio, is an entrepreneur, philanthropist and the wife of NBA superstar LeBron James.Savannah and LeBron met while they were in high school and have remained together since then. They married in 2013 and have three children: Bronny, Bryce and Zhuri.While her family is closely associated with LeBron’s basketball career, Savannah has developed her own interests and projects. She has been involved in charitable and community initiatives, with a particular focus on education and women’s empowerment.She played a key role in launching the LeBron James Family Foundation and founded Women of Our Future, a mentorship program supporting young women in Akron.Savannah has also worked in design and interior decorating while developing interests in fashion and wellness. Her investment in LOVB Los Angeles adds another sports-related business venture to that wider portfolio.Zhuri Nova James is the youngest child of LeBron and Savannah James. She was born on Oct. 22, 2014, after her parents had already welcomed sons Bronny and Bryce.LeBron has spoken warmly about his daughter and the role she plays in his life.“My daughter is the greatest thing in my life, along with my boys,” LeBron told Access Hollywood in 2021. “So, whenever she smiles, it don't matter what I'm doing, it makes me happy.”Zhuri has grown up in the spotlight and has appeared alongside her family at events and in campaigns. She attended the ESPY Awards, accompanied LeBron to the premiere of Space Jam: A New Legacy and appeared in a 2023 Beats by Dre campaign with her family.She has also explored fashion. In 2020, Zhuri helped launch the Janie and Jack x Harlem's Fashion Row collection and spoke about her excitement surrounding the project.“I’m most excited about the fashion and talking to the designers,” she told PEOPLE. Zhuri also revealed that she had “practiced with” her mother, Savannah.Away from fashion, she launched an Instagram account and YouTube channel. Her YouTube series, All Things Zhuri, included videos featuring her interests, with LeBron appearing in one episode.But volleyball has emerged as the clearest sporting connection for Savannah’s daughter. LeBron has shared videos of Zhuri playing, including one in 2023 in which he cheered her on.“Another One in the making! Uh-Oh 😱!!” LeBron captioned a carousel of videos. “Let’s Gooooooo Munchin!! @allthingszhuri got NEXT!! 🏐 VIBES!! #JamesGang👑 #ZTheWarriorPrincess👸🏾.”That path now has a direct connection to Savannah’s latest investment. As LOVB Los Angeles prepares for its first season, Zhuri’s passion for volleyball has helped give her mother a personal reason to become part of the league’s next chapter.
Article Summary: Lebron james’ daughter zhuri inspired savannah james to invest in women’s volleyball. Savannah is joining an ownership group led by reddit co-founder alexis ohanian through his investment firm, seven seven six. The investment comes ahead of lovb los angeles’ first season. The team is scheduled to begin play during the league’s 2026-27 season.

Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s charity implements new ways to help children in Oakland

Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, and his wife, Ayesha Curry , have always been passionate about helping out children in their hometown, Oakland. Both of them have remained dedicated to the cause for close to a decade now. Their recent efforts have earned them millions in funding for their charity, Eat, Learn & Play.A few days ago, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s charity took to their social media to make a post highlighting what the high profile couple have been busy doing in the offseason.In the clip, Stephen Curry says, “We’re here at the seventh annual Workday Charity Classic benefitting Eat, Learn & Play. It’s been an amazing journey raising over $10 million through this event for the work Eat, Learn, Play is doing.”The four time NBA champion added, “So, excited to have another day on the course raising a lot of money supporting a lot of kids, continuing to broaden the horizons of what Eat, Learn, Play’s impact can be in Oakland.”The clip then goes on to show Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, trying their hand at golf while they interact with their guests and speak about their charity’s impact in Oakland.The caption of the post read as, “What a great day on the course! For the seventh year, the Workday Charity Classic has brought @eatlearnplay friends and supporters together to support Oakland kids.Every dollar raised helps provide nutritious food, quality reading resources, and opportunities to play and be active.”The caption added, “The event wouldn’t have been possible without the generosity of our host, @workday, along with our village of partners and supporters. Together we are uplifting a generation of Oakland students. #ELPCoFounders #WorkdayPartner”Founded in 2016, Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry’s charity Eat, Learn & Play has been able to raise over $100 million in the last decade.Both the NBA legend Stephen Curry and his wife Ayesha Curry have remained committed to the cause of helping children coming from underprivileged families in Oakland.The main vision behind the charity has been to provide nutritious meals and quality education to Oakland’s children.But now, Eat, Learn & Play, has gone beyond it as it has continued to change millions of lives across the state.The charity has recorded more participation in middle school sports and has also been able to build several playgrounds for schools in the last few years.While both Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, lead busy lives, they have remained closely associated with the cause behind their foundation in Oakland.

Article Title: Lakshya Sen’s eight-point comeback powers India into Asian Games badminton semis
Article Text:
Lakshya Sen

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When India needed him most, Lakshya Sen rediscovered his fighting spirit.Battling injuries and a prolonged slump in form, the Almora shuttler produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of his career, clawing back from 13-19 down in the deciding game against Japan’s Kodai Naraoka to win eight points in a row and seal a stunning victory in the men’s team quarterfinal.That win powered India into the semi-finals as the men swept the host nation 3-0 to assure a second consecutive team medal. The result followed the Indian women’s exit from the competition as they lost 1-3 to the hosts.India had gone into the tie with real concern over the recent form of its top-ranked singles player coming into the Games. Facing a formidable Japanese lineup, the team needed Lakshya to deliver, with the doubles pairing of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, and the young Ayush Shetty, expected to take care of their respective ties.Lakshya, however, had to dig deep before producing his moment of magic.Trailing 13-19 in the decider, he reeled off eight consecutive points to stun Naraoka 11-21, 21-5, 21-19.Satwik and Chirag made it 2-0 for India with a hard-fought win over former world champions Takuro Hoki and Yugo Kobayashi. Ayush then moved India to the brink of victory with a straight-games win over Koki Watanabe, 21-10, 21-19.But the story of the day belonged to Lakshya.He looked out of sorts in the opening game, moving poorly around the court and lacking his usual aggression. A pep talk from chief coach Pullela Gopichand appeared to change the complexion of the contest.Lakshya returned for the second game with renewed energy and immediately took control, racing to a 7-1 lead and never allowing Naraoka to recover as he wrapped up the game 21-5.The momentum shifted again in the decider. Naraoka steadily built an advantage and was sitting comfortably at 19-13, just two points from victory. With India’s hopes resting on him, Lakshya produced the best stretch of the match.At 14-19, he took the risk of playing a cross-court smash to Naraoka’s forehand and followed it with another winner into the backhand corner. The Japanese shuttler then hit into the net before misjudging a line call, allowing Lakshya to draw level at 19-19.At 19-all, Lakshya produced another moment of brilliance, diving full length to retrieve a drop shot and push the shuttle towards the backline to earn match point at 20-19. Naraoka then erred at the net.“It was a memorable victory. Great to see the singles players and Satwik-Chirag win another medal for India. With two Asian Games medals, two Thomas Cup medals and two Badminton Asia medals, it has been a dream period for us. I am confident our team will go the distance,” chief coach Pullela Gopichand told TOI.India will face China in the semi-finals after the latter defeated South Korea 3-2. Indonesia will take on Thailand.The Indian women’s team saw its campaign end against Japan.World Championships bronze medallists Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand secured India’s lone point with a 21-17, 21-16 win over Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto. PV Sindhu lost the opening singles to Akane Yamaguchi 23-21, 18-21, 11-21, while Unnati Hooda went down to Tomoka Miyazaki 16-21, 18-21, leaving Japan 2-0 ahead.Tanvi Sharma then lost the crucial fourth tie to Nozomi Okuhara 12-21, 10-21.The women’s semi-finals will see South Korea face Japan and China play Indonesia.
Article Summary: Lakshya sen produced one of the most dramatic comebacks of his career. He fought back from 13-19 down in the deciding game against japan’s kodai naraoka to win eight points in a row. That win powered india into the semi-finals as the men swept the host nation 3-0 to assure a second consecutive team medal.

Article Title: Harmanpreet’s India make history with record 147-run win, clinch Asian Games gold
Article Text:
Asian Games: Women's cricket delivers first gold medal

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Trust the women to lead the way. Proud to be part of the Indian contingent at the Asian Games, but with no athletes’ village and handed a tight schedule, the women’s cricket team had little opportunity to mingle with, interact with or watch the country’s other athletes.But on a sun-kissed Tuesday at the Korogi Sports Park here, Harmanpreet Kaur and her team gave the nearly 500-strong contingent a big reason to celebrate, winning India’s first gold of the Games with a dominant 147-run win, the highest margin of victory by runs in women’s T20 Internationals, over Sri Lanka in the final.The skipper was delighted that her team had struck India’s first gold.“It’s a big thing for me because our aim was to take back the gold. More importantly, we wanted to see our flag fly high. We didn’t think we would win the first gold. I’m sure our athletes will win many more gold medals,” Harmanpreet said.Unlike the other events they play in, there is no trophy to be lifted here. But Harmanpreet was more than happy to trade it for a gold medal.“When we win trophies, they go to the BCCI office,” she said with a laugh. “The biggest thing for us is to be part of the Games and take back a medal to frame and keep at home,” Harmanpreet said.The gold was not just a successful defence of a medal. It was a reminder, on an evening when their fellow athletes were scattered across the city and beyond, that the contingent could come together in celebration.“Looking at the overall calendar and our list of achievements, as cricketers, we always wanted to be part of the Asian Games, Commonwealth Games and the Olympics. We have always played bilateral series, the ICC World Cup and Asia Cup, but until the previous Asian Games, we didn’t know what it felt like to work hard for a medal. We feel lucky that we are getting these opportunities now. So we just want to take the positives from this. ”In a rematch of the previous edition of the Asian Games, India put up a commanding 216/3 before skittling out Sri Lanka for 69 in 15.4 overs on a ‘hybrid’ pitch that aided spinners. Smriti Mandhana led the charge with a 45-ball 79, hitting five fours and seven sixes, while Shafali Verma made 48 off 29 balls (3x4; 3x6).Richa Ghosh then provided the late fireworks, smashing an unbeaten 49 off just 22 balls.In reply, Sri Lanka struggled to cope with the turning track. Deepti Sharma led India’s spin quartet with 3/6, while Shafali (2/3), Shreyanka Patil (2/9) and Shree Charani (2/13) claimed two wickets apiece.On a surface that initially offered plenty to the batters, Shafali and Smriti needed little time to settle. Smriti opened her account with consecutive boundaries through point off Sugandika Kumari, and after Mithali Ayodhya kept Shafali quiet for an over, Smriti took the attack back to Sugandika with back-to-back sixes.The two then cleared the ropes with regularity before Chamudi Praboda broke the partnership, Shafali’s reverse sweep finding Kawya Kavindi at backward point.But the damage had been done. Smriti appeared set for a century before miscuing a slog sweep off Sugandika Kumari. Richa took over, adding the finishing flourish that lifted India past 200.Sri Lanka never got going in the chase. Apart from skipper Chamari Athapaththu, who made 29, and Kaushini Nuthyangana (14), none of their batters managed to reach double figures.As soon as Shreyanka rattled Kaushini Nuthyangana’s stumps to seal the gold, the tricolour began fluttering in the team dugout. Moments later, the players held it aloft in celebration.BRIEF SCORES: India 216/3 (Mandhana 79, Ghosh 49*, Shafali 48, Praboda 1-34) beat Sri Lanka 69 (Athapaththu 29, Deepti 3-6, Shafali 2-3, Patil 2-9, Charani 2-13) by 147 runs.
Article Summary: India beat sri lanka by 147 runs in women's t20 internationals final. Smriti mandhana and shafali verma top scored with 79 and 48 respectively. India put up 216/3 before skittling out sri lanka for 69 in 15.4 overs on 'hybrid' pitch. Apart from skipper chamari athapaththu, who made 29, and kaushini nuthyangana (14), none of their batters managed to reach double figures.

Article Title: Elavenil Valarivan, Parth Mane miss podium after late charge falls short in 10m air rifle mixed event
Article Text:
The team of Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Mane finished fourth in the final of 10m air rifle mixed event at Asian Games 2026

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagoya: The smiles on Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Mane’s faces as they left the qualification arena for the 10m air rifle mixed event made way for agony after the first five shots of the final at the Aichi Prefectural Shooting Range.On Tuesday, from bettering the Games record and finishing second in the qualifiers to ending fourth, well short of the podium, the result came down to consistency, or the lack of it.The shooters, who won silver medals over the past two days, were on point in the qualifiers with 634.6, behind China (638.9). Both teams bettered the Games qualification record, which stood at 634.4.In the final, Japan took the last spot after Vietnam were disqualified because their competition suits failed to meet international standards.After the first five shots, India were last with 103.6, 0.3 behind the hosts. They played catch-up, by which time Korea, who finished third, had taken a two-point lead.Elavenil and Mane made a late charge but failed to bridge the gap, finishing with 376.3. China took the gold with a world record of 507.1, while Korea and Japan settled for silver and bronze.The rifle team’s coach, Pooja Ghatkar, pinned the performance on inconsistency.“Elavenil did well in the qualification. But both shooters were not able to settle into their positions in the final and their shots were all over the place,” she said.She also felt the timeout strategy misfired.
Article Summary: The team of elavenil valarivan and parth mane finished fourth in the final of 10m air rifle mixed event at asian games 2026. China took the gold with a world record of 507.1, while korea and japan settled for silver and bronze. India were last with 103.6, 0.3 behind the hosts.

Article Title: Mirabai Chanu wins maiden Asian Games medal, bags silver in 49kg category

NEW DELHI: India's star weightlifter Mirabai Chanu won her maiden Asian Games medal on Wednesday, claiming silver medal in the women's 49kg category at the Nagoya City Trade and Industry Center in Aichi and Nagoya.Mirabai lifted a total of 198 kg in the event. She lifted 87 kg in the snatch before managing 111 kg in the clean and jerk to finish with the silver medal.North Korea's Ri Song Gum won the gold medal with a total lift of 215kg. In the 49kg weight class, she set Commonwealth Games records in the snatch, clean and jerk and overall categories at the 2018 edition, before bettering those marks at the 2022 and 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: A 97-year-old Brisbane bowls club facing demolition is saved in a $6 million deal after Bowls Queensland rejected an offer $1 million higher to keep both greens
Article Text:
Griffin Hospitality plans to renovate the clubhouse, bar and kitchen while retaining the atmosphere and character associated with the club. The aim is to make the venue more welcoming for bowlers, families and visitors while keeping the sport at its centre.

A campaign that kept the greens alive

Plans for a renewed clubhouse

The committee stays on

For a club that spent years staring down the prospect of demolition, the future of Coorparoo Bowls Club now looks very different. The 97-year-old Brisbane institution will remain a place for bowls and community gatherings after the site was sold for $6 million to a local investor, ending plans that could have replaced the club with high-rise apartments, states the latest news report by ABC News. The deal preserves both bowling greens and gives the historic club a chance to enter its next chapter without losing the character that has defined it for generations.As per the ABC News report, the sale follows a multi-year campaign by the Coorparoo Bowls Club committee, which had been fighting to protect the venue and was facing eviction in May this year. Rather than see the site disappear under a redevelopment, the club will now remain in place under new ownership. Bowls Queensland reached the $6 million agreement with Coorparoo local Will Griffin of Griffin Hospitality Group after considering competing offers. The organisation rejected an offer that was $1 million higher, prioritising an agreement that would keep bowls operating at the site.That decision means both existing greens will stay. One will be available for competitions, while the other will cater to casual players, preserving the club's role for both organised games and everyday community use.The new ownership is expected to bring changes to the venue, but not a complete transformation, adds the online report. Griffin Hospitality plans to renovate the clubhouse, bar and kitchen while retaining the atmosphere and character associated with the club. The aim is to make the venue more welcoming for bowlers, families and visitors while keeping the sport at its centre. The plans also position the club as more than a sporting venue, with space for meals, social gatherings and community activities alongside regular bowls. For a property that had been facing a very different future, the approach offers a way to modernise the venue without erasing its history.The report also states that the committee that led the campaign to save Coorparoo Bowls Club will remain involved, signing a five-year lease to continue running the club. That arrangement keeps the people who have helped steer the club through its uncertain years connected to its future. With both greens protected, renovations planned and the existing committee remaining at the helm, Coorparoo Bowls Club has avoided demolition and secured a path forward. After nearly a century at the heart of the local community, the club will continue rolling bowls rather than making way for towers.Image Courtesy: ABC News
Article Summary: Coorparoo bowls club has been sold for $6 million to a local investor. The deal preserves both bowling greens and gives the historic club a chance to enter its next chapter without losing the character that has defined it for generations. Griffin hospitality plans to renovate the clubhouse, bar and kitchen while retaining the atmosphere and character associated with the club.

Article Title: ‘We want to see him under pressure’: New Zealand coach lays down challenge for Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
Article Text:
Vaibhav Sooryavanshi

New Zealand head coach Rob Walter is keen to see how India’s teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi handles the challenge of pace and bounce when the two sides meet in the upcoming T20I series.Sooryavanshi has already made a name for himself with explosive performances in the IPL in 2025 and 2026, as well as at this year’s U19 World Cup. Those displays earned him his T20I debut against England in July.The teenager was part of India’s squad for the 3-0 T20I series win over Afghanistan and the narrow two-run victory over Japan in Sano, but did not feature in the playing eleven.Walter said he would be particularly interested in watching Sooryavanshi bat on the seam-friendly, bouncy New Zealand surfaces and also see how he responds if put under pressure.“Yes, I'd love to see him on some pace in bouncy wickets and see how different that looks. But he's an exciting player. You've seen him dominate against the world's best bowlers in the IPL. I think the challenge is always to see how that translates to different conditions and also how do we bowl to him in our conditions.“Again, secretly as a coach, you always want to see your players under a little bit of pressure and how we respond to that.So looking forward to it, if that is the case. If he's not here, they do have a lot of very good players other than him,” Walter told reporters on Wednesday.The New Zealand coach was also asked about the controversial wide call during India’s recent one-off T20I against Japan, which sparked considerable debate.Walter made it clear that he had not followed the match closely and had little interest in getting drawn into the controversy.“A very short segment (I watched). I saw there was some controversy around the wide ruling. But no, I didn't watch a hell of a lot of it, to be fair. The lesser the better, I think.”The upcoming series will also bring New Zealand back together for their first T20I engagement as a collective since the T20 World Cup final in Ahmedabad, where they suffered a heavy defeat to India.Walter acknowledged that losing a final naturally leaves a mark, but insisted the Black Caps' motivation for the home series is not centred on revenge.“I suppose it is there. No one likes to lose a final. I've done it twice, so I know all about it. But I think what comes first is representing the Black Caps and New Zealand well. So you've got a group of players who are always trying to do that first. Of course, if you manage to get a couple of victories at home, that would be great.“But taking care of the little steps in between now and then is the most important part. Being excited about representing again - it's been a while for some of the guys. Obviously it's the first time as a collective since the World Cup, with the majority of the squad that was in the World Cup to run out together.“So there's always something in it. It's not our major focal point, certainly not the things we speak about the most. Most importantly, we want to play good cricket and represent well,” he explained.
Article Summary: Vaibhav sooryavanshi has already made a name for himself with explosive performances in the ipl in 2025 and 2026. The teenager was part of india’s squad for the 3-0 t20i series win over afghanistan and the narrow two-run victory over japan in sano, but did not feature in the playing eleven.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El rubius was eliminated from mrbeast's $1 million challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

But for a 25-year-old techie the craze for IPL tickets for RCB vs CSK turned too costly and he was duped for a massive Rs. 1.46 lakh.The techie, a resident of B Narayanapura, fell into a trap by a post posted by a fraudster who posed himself as a ticket seller on Instagram.As per a report in Deccan Herald, the techie alleged in a complaint to Mahadevapura Police that an individual claiming to be Sumit Biswal promised he could arrange IPL tickets along with food coupons.As per the techie, Biswal was introduced him as a senior supervisor for ticket counter at M Chinnaswamy Stadium"He asked me to come near the stadium gate number 10, saying someone would deliver the tickets within minutes, and even sent an email confirmation to gain my trust," the complainant told Deccan Herald."Initially, I agreed to buy two tickets for Rs 3,700 each,but he kept asking for more money under various pretexts such as refundable security deposits, additional ID cards and food coupons.Trusting him, I made multiple payments - even using my mother’s bank account after exhausting my own limits—and ended up transferring around Rs 1.46 lakh," he added.Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s incisive spell of 3-41, coming after a marauding batting show from Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal, propelled Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) to a commanding 43-run victory over Chennai Super Kings (CSK) in their IPL 2026 encounter at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium on Sunday.The contest saw RCB’s batting unit dismantle CSK’s attack with relentless hitting, as David’s 70 not out off just 25 balls and Patidar’s unbeaten 48 off only 19 balls provided for the late fireworks after Padikkal’s fluent 50 off 29 balls had set the tone for the daunting total.Their combined effort lifted RCB to a daunting 250/3, thus setting a new record for highest total in IPL 2026. Article Title: In 2007, Scottish cyclist Mark Beaumont left Paris to race around Earth; 194 days and 17 hours later, crashes, theft and exhaustion had not stopped him
Article Text:
Scottish adventurer Mark Beaumont is pictured during his long-distance cycling career and carrying the Olympic torch during the London Olympics torch relay. Beaumont carried the flame across the Forth Road Bridge in Scotland. Credits - Wikipedia

A path through hardship

Mark Beaumont cycles alongside a local rider and a donkey-drawn cart in eastern Pakistan during his 2007–08 record-setting journey around the world by bicycle. Credits - Wikipedia

Rewriting the record

Long before ultra-endurance sport became a global spectacle, crossing the world on two wheels was the domain of the odd and the dreamer. Record keepers had been tracking efforts at this achievement for decades, and the bar kept moving as riders pushed further into the unknown with little more than paper maps, panniers and persistence. A young man from rural Fife, a man who had spent his childhood cycling throughout Scotland for enjoyment, stepped into that bloodline in the summer of 2007. What came next would see him become one of the defining figures in endurance riding and rewrite what people thought was physically feasible on a bicycle.On 5 August 2007, Mark Beaumont left the Arc de Triomphe in Paris on a laden touring bike with an objective that appeared almost reckless for someone who had never attempted anything on this scale before. He planned to ride about 100 miles a day, alone and unsupported, until he had travelled round the globe and got back to where he started. His bicycle, a Koga Miyata with a Rohloff internal gear hub, was loaded with around 30 kilogrammes of tools, spare parts and video equipment, since he was chronicling the voyage himself for what would become a BAFTA nominated BBC film. Cycling UK , the membership club that has long backed British riders on just this sort of personal endeavour, later published his own report of how three years of planning went into that single departure from Paris.Beaumont’s journey carried him east via Europe and Russia, through Central Asia and the Indian subcontinent, across Southeast Asia and Australia, and then across North America before one more trans-Atlantic trip back to France. It was a tough trail, and preparation wouldn’t make it easier. In Lafayette, Louisiana, he was hit by a car and robbed later that same day, an experience that would have killed most people’s endeavours on the spot. Elsewhere he fought illness and the sort of physical disintegration that comes from sixteen or more hours a day in the saddle for months on end without rest. He’d also meant to be a vegetarian but had little choice but to give that up during the ride simply to keep enough calories going in to survive the daily mileage.It’s not only the distance but also the isolation that makes the achievement exceptional. Throughout the ride, Beaumont had no support car, no mechanic and no chef. If his gear broke or his body let him down, he had to tackle the problem himself, often in isolated parts of Pakistan, Iran or the Australian outback where help was hours or days away. He used paper maps in an age when smartphone navigation didn’t even exist for bikes and had his mother back home assist him in plotting alternative routes if roads were blocked.On 15 February 2008, Beaumont cycled back past the Arc de Triomphe, having completed almost 18,000 miles in 194 days and 17 hours. That broke the previous world record by 81 days, a margin so vast that even veteran endurance athletes who had thought the mark would stand for years were startled. His accomplishment was officially validated, and the lineage of riders who chased and ultimately beat his time is still recorded on the official Guinness World Records page for the quickest circumnavigation by bicycle. Other cyclists would eventually beat Beaumont's own record, such as Vin Cox in 2010, before Beaumont himself recaptured the supported version of the championship in 2017 with a specially organised support squad, further lowering his own original time.But it is the 2007 solo ride that attracted public attention, because he did it without a safety net. Beaumont then returned to his old university, the University of St Andrews , to speak to students about the trip. He didn't frame it as some prank, but as proof that ordinary preparedness, stubbornness and a tolerance for discomfort might take a person further than nearly anyone expected. The ride raised £18,000 for charity and he utilised the platform it established to launch a series of additional expeditions including the length of the Americas trip from Alaska to Argentina and a solo unsupported crossing from Cairo to Cape Town.Nearly two decades later, Beaumont's original circumnavigation is still cited as a moment when unsupported round-the-world cycling moved from an oddity to a recognised branch of endurance sport, inspiring later solo riders like Jenny Graham and a wave of amateur cyclists who attempt similar routes every year. It’s not just the miles that keep the story alive, but what it said about the extremes individuals will reach when curiosity and discipline collide.
Article Summary: Mark beaumont left the arc de triomphe in paris on a laden touring bike in august 2007. He planned to ride about 100 miles a day, alone and unsupported, until he had travelled round the globe and got back to where he started. His bicycle, a koga miyata with a rohloff internal gear hub, was loaded with around 30 kilogrammes of tools, spare parts and video equipment.

Article Title: BGMI Gully Wars announced: Registration deadline, qualifier dates and prize pool
Article Text:
BGMI Gully Wars is here

BGMI Gully Wars qualifiers begin October 14, with 16 teams set to reach the finals

Krafton India has announced BGMI Gully Wars, a new open-for-all Battlegrounds Mobile India (BGMI) tournament with a prize pool of Rs 10 lakh. Registrations are live now and will close on October 6. There is no entry barrier for prior competitive experience, so any squad can sign up.The idea is to find players who are good but largely unknown. Many BGMI players are known only within their own squads, college groups or local Discord servers, and rarely get a proper shot at organised play. Gully Wars, which runs on the tagline "Apna Naam Bana", is pitched as that first step. The tournament is being organised in partnership with JioBLAST.The competition opens with an In-Game Qualifier running from October 14 to 20. Teams that make it through will move into a series of elimination rounds, which cut the field down to the final 16 teams for the Grand Finals. Dates for the later stages and the prize split have not been detailed yet.Karan Pathak, Associate Director - Esports, Krafton India, said the tournament is aimed at the next generation of competitive players."We look forward to seeing players from across the country step up, make their mark and, most importantly, make their name," he said.To register, players need to visit kraftonindiaesports.com and click the BGMI Gully Wars banner, or head to the Tournaments section and select "Register Now". First-time users will have to create an account, while existing users can log in with their credentials or through OTP verification. Tournament updates and announcements will be shared on the Krafton India Esports and JioBLAST Instagram handles.For squads that have so far only tested themselves in custom rooms with friends, this is a straightforward way to see how they stack up nationally. The deadline to get in is October 6.

Article Title: Nike Alphafly 4 launched with lighter ZoomX LT foam and 10% more energy return
Article Text:
Nike Alphafly 4 are 5% lighter than Alphafly 3

Two foams now sandwich the plate

The upper is designed for tired feet

Nike has launched the Alphafly 4, the newest version of its marathon racing shoe, with changes to nearly every major part. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5.The biggest change is in the midsole. Nike has added a new ZoomX LT foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard ZoomX and offers 8% more energy return. The shoe goes on early, limited sale on nike.com from today, September 17, with wider availability on nike.com and at select stores from October 29.ZoomX LT doesn't fully replace regular ZoomX. Nike layers the two foams above and below the carbon-fibre Flyplate, which keeps the Alphafly's signature propulsive scoop. The plate adds stability and guides a smooth forward roll, which should help runners hold a steady cadence. Up front, dual Air Zoom units have been retuned to work alongside the foam and plate at push-off. A lightweight Fast Shot outsole handles grip.The new Atomknit upper is seamless and breathable. It uses zoned midfoot cables, an integrated heel unit and a molded sock liner to hold the foot securely over long distances.Nike says development drew on athlete feedback across Alphafly generations, learnings from Project Dreamweaver, and extensive women's trials. Emily Farina, Senior Principal, Running Footwear, Nike Sport Research Lab, said the team studied how fatigue changes running mechanics."Our goal was simple: create a shoe that helps athletes feel more confident and capable deep into the race," she said.Nike athlete Addisu Gobena has already tested that claim. He wore the Alphafly 4 to a course-record marathon win in Sydney, and said he trusted the shoe when the race got difficult.
Article Summary: Nike alphafly 4 is the newest version of its marathon racing shoe. The company says it returns 10% more energy than its predecessor and weighs 5% less in a men's size 8.5. Nike has added a new zoomx lt foam, which it says is up to 17% lighter than standard zoomx.

Article Title: Rockstar Games spends nearly $1 million on ‘Welcome to Vice City’ sign for GTA 6 marketing: Report
Article Text:
Image via Rockstar Games

Rockstar installs GTA 6 sign at Kaseya Center

How long will the GTA 6 sign stay

Rockstar Games is taking its Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6) marketing campaign to Miami, with the company reportedly spending nearly $1 million on a giant “Welcome to Vice City” sign installed on top of the Kaseya Center. The sign, which was lifted into place by a helicopter, is part of Rockstar’s wider marketing push for the highly anticipated game. According to Miami Herald journalist Doug Hanks, Miami-Dade is expected to collect $975,000 from Rockstar under a marketing agreement.“Miami-Dade set to collect $975,000 from the Vice City lettering going up on the county-owned Kaseya Center, per the agreement with GTA maker Rockstar Games,” the journalist wrote in an X post.The giant “Welcome to Vice City” sign was recently installed on the roof of the Kaseya Center, home of the Miami Heat. Fans had been watching the sign being constructed in recent days. It was eventually lifted to the top of the arena by helicopter and installed on the roof.According to Miami Herald journalist Doug Hanks, Rockstar is paying just under $1 million for the installation. Miami-Dade is expected to receive $975,000 as part of the marketing agreement.The sign may be only one part of Rockstar's plans for promoting GTA 6 in the city. The company reportedly held discussions with Miami officials in August about several possible marketing activities. These included events and even a possible takeover of the airport.Documents reviewed by IGN reportedly say the sign will remain on the arena for “the latter of one year after” installation or until the final Miami Heat home game of the 2026-27 season. That game is scheduled for April 11, 2027, meaning the GTA 6 sign could remain visible through the rest of 2026 and into next spring.The documents also set an October 15 deadline for installing the sign. The date could become another GTA 6 marketing moment, although Rockstar has not confirmed this.Grand Theft Auto 6 will launch on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
Article Summary: Rockstar games is taking its grand theft auto 6 (gta 6) marketing campaign to miami. NEW DELHI: Shubman Gill-led India ODI squad for the three-match series against West Indies is set to assemble in Thiruvananthapuram by Thursday (September 24). Some players will reach the venue for the series opener on Wednesday night, while the rest will link up a day later.The series will see Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma back in action, while Ravindra Jadeja will return to the format after being omitted from the fixtures following the ODI series against New Zealand earlier this year. Most of India's first-choice ODI players, vice-captain Shreyas Iyer, Ishan Kishan, Jasprit Bumrah and Axar Patel, are on Asian Games duty in Japan. Their absence opened up slots for players like Ruturaj Gaikwad, Auqib Nabi and even the experienced Jadeja.With Hardik Pandya unavailable for selection, the selectors withdrew Nitish Kumar Reddy from the Asian Games because they are keen to give the young all-rounder game time to build and maintain his bowling volume. Head coach Gautam Gambhir asserted after the T20Is against Afghanistan that Reddy will improve when he bowls more in international cricket and even hinted at the possibility of playing both him and Pandya in the XI."From Nitish's point of view, it's actually a great thing that he's been withdrawn from the T20 format, and he'll get game time against the West Indies as well. We know how important a seam-bowling all-rounder will probably be in a year, and when we go to South Africa. And once Hardik comes back, obviously it's going to be good. Sometimes we could even go on to play both of them in the playing 11," said Gambhir.The series is also important for KL Rahul to again cement his position as the first-choice wicketkeeper-bat in the ODI set-up. The think tank has explored using Ishan Kishan by giving him game time and even the big gloves, but Rahul's consistency in this format has been right up there, and his experience will be invaluable in South African conditions. KL Rahul is currently training at the Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru to prepare for the ODI series.The West Indies team has already landed and will commence preparations for the series.Shubman Gill (captain), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Ruturaj Gaikwad, KL Rahul (vice-captain), Dhruv Jurel, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Ravindra Jadeja, Kuldeep Yadav, Prasidh Krishna, Gurnoor Brar, Mohammed Siraj, Auqib Nabi, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Naman Dhir.Shai Hope (captain), Jewel Andrew, John Campbell, Keacy Carty, Roston Chase, Matthew Forde, Justin Greaves, Amir Jangoo, Alzarri Joseph, Shamar Joseph, Vitel Lawes, Gudakesh Motie, Keemo Paul, Sherfane Rutherford, Jayden Seales.
